source.section: Head of Household schedule, 1.95% band; Form ND-1 lines 1b, 4b, 17, 18, 19, 20, 24, 25; booklet PDF p.4 (starting point is federal taxable income), PDF p.13 Line 1b, PDF p.16 Line 20, PDF p.29 Tax Rate Schedules, PDF pp.22-28 Tax Table

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 100,000.00 = 100,000.00. Federal taxable income = 100,000.00 - standard deduction 23,625.00 = 76,375.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form ND-1 line 1b federal taxable income 76,375.00; lines 2-3 additions 0.00, line 4a 0.00; line 4b = 76,375.00. Subtractions lines 5-16: none; line 17 = 0.00. Line 18 North Dakota taxable income = 76,375.00 - 0.00 = 76,375.00. Line 19 = 76,375.00. Line 20 tax: 1.95% x (76,375.00 - 64,950.00) = 1.95% x 11,425.00 = 222.7875, to the cent 222.79; the Tax Table row 76,350 to 76,400 gives 223; expected uses the bracket formula on the exact income. Lines 21-23 credits: line 22 marriage penalty credit: not a joint return, so none. Expected credits 0.00. Line 25 net tax = 222.79.
accepted_approximations: Tax below 100,000 is figured on the exact income; the booklet uses a 50-dollar Tax Table row rounded to whole dollars.
